strings.meta.title: sintr — a private mood diary for the week between therapy sessions
strings.meta.description: sintr is a private mood diary you keep by talking to your AI assistant. Before each therapy session, your week is waiting on one page, in your own words, shared with your therapist only if you say so. It stays on your own computer.

strings.why.b: Your week happens in the rest of it.
strings.why.body: By the session, Tuesday is a blur. You remember how you feel today, and what shook you midweek never quite gets told.
strings.capture.title: Tuesday, 7:40 pm. Tell it while it's fresh.
strings.capture.body: You tell your assistant what happened, the way you'd tell a friend. It asks one or two questions, then saves it.
strings.capture.quiet: On ordinary days, one line is enough.
strings.capture.chat_label: Example conversation with an AI assistant
strings.capture.msg1: Can we write down what happened at planning? I'm still wound up.
strings.capture.msg2: Of course. What went through your mind right then, and how strong was the anxiety, from 0 to 100?
strings.capture.msg3: “There's no way I can handle this.” About 85.
strings.capture.msg4: Saved. We can look at that thought more closely now, or leave it for your session.
strings.report.title: Monday, 5 pm. The week comes together.
strings.report.body: An hour before your session, your assistant turns it into a short PDF: how the week went, what you want to talk about, a chart of your mood and sleep, and the moments that stood out, in your own words. Patterns are noted as observations, never as diagnoses.

strings.report.doc_title: October 12–18. Demo Person's week, in their own words.
strings.report.doc_week: A heavy week at work. The two hardest moments came early: Tuesday's planning, when three new demands landed at once, and Thursday's feedback conversation. Friday brought the best moment: a walk at lunch without the phone, the first in weeks.
strings.report.doc_session2: The Sunday afternoon anxiety, back for a second Sunday in a row.
strings.report.doc_moment1: Tue, Oct 13 — Planning, three new demands in one sprint: “there's no way I can handle this”. Anxiety 85. Accepted all three on the spot.
strings.report.doc_moment2: Fri, Oct 16 — A walk at lunch without the phone: “first time in weeks I stopped in the middle of the day”. Relief 60.
strings.report.doc_pattern1: Oct 11 and 18 — Late on Sunday afternoon, anxiety and the same thought: “tomorrow it all starts again”.
strings.report.doc_foot: Prepared from self-reports with the help of a personal assistant, and reviewed by Demo Person before sending. Observations, not diagnoses. Not a clinical assessment.
strings.report.source: Abridged from a fictional example; the full report is a four-page PDF. This person writes in Portuguese, so their report does too; yours comes out in your language.
strings.report.step1_text: Read the PDF and change anything. It's your week.
strings.report.step2_text: Only an explicit “send it” sends it. It never happens on its own.
strings.report.step3_text: The same PDF goes to your therapist, the way you chose, with a note of who got it and when.
strings.report.payoff: Monday, 6 pm. The hour starts with Tuesday, not with today.
strings.privacy.title: Your thoughts stay yours.
strings.privacy.p1_text: A folder, like a notebook in a drawer. No app, no account, no cloud.
strings.privacy.p2_text: Other people using the same computer can't open it.
strings.privacy.p3_text: Nothing is copied into chats or other services, and deleting means deleting.
strings.privacy.note: One thing to know: the AI assistant you talk to usually sends what you type to the company behind it. Choose one you're comfortable with. Technical details
strings.start.title: Start in three steps.
strings.start.intro: You need an AI assistant that runs on your computer and can save files there, like Claude Code, Hermes, OpenCode or OpenClaw. Browser-only chats can't. Claude Cowork needs one extra manual step, described on the technical page.
strings.start.step1_text: It's written for your assistant: where to get sintr and how to set it up.
strings.start.step2_text: It sets everything up and explains each step. It may ask permission first; that's normal.
strings.start.step3_text: Your language, time zone, therapist and session day. Then just talk to it when you need to.
strings.start.summary: Read the setup message before you copy it
strings.start.message: Please set up sintr for me. It's a private journal for therapy that you'll keep for me as files on this computer. Clone https://github.com/tiagomoraes/sintr.git, read docs/INSTALL.md, and run the installer that matches you (./installers/install.sh with hermes, claude-code or generic), using ~/sintr as my journal folder. Explain each step to me in plain words before you do it. Then open ~/sintr/config.md and fill it in with me: ask for my language, time zone and therapy details one at a time, and leave empty anything I don't give you. Keep require_approval: true, and never send anything to anyone without asking me first.
strings.start.message_foot: It only uses what's published in the sintr project.
strings.honest.body: It isn't therapy, a diagnosis or an emergency service. It won't label you or tell you what to do.
strings.lines.title: If you're in danger or thinking about harming yourself, please call someone now.
strings.lines.l1_who: CVV, Centro de Valorização da VidaFree, 24 hours
strings.lines.l2_who: 988 crisis lineCall or text, 24 hours
strings.lines.l4_who: SNS 24Health line with psychological support
strings.lines.note: Anywhere else, call your local emergency number or find a free, confidential line near you at findahelpline.com. If you tell your assistant you're at risk, sintr asks it to stop taking notes and help you find someone right away.
